bot_cpu_scope: Each worker Python process plus reaped native SearchWorker descendants, including startup and preparation. Simulator/coordinator CPU is excluded. Native elapsed milliseconds are measured wall time, not CPU.
native_world_concurrency: One thread per native search, sequential worlds within each bot. A game coordinator currently waits for one side choice at a time. Each screening batch runs at most four games.

normal_active_screening_cap.tail_overlap_rule: sum(min(4, remaining planned games) over old active batches) <= 4 before admitting a new four-game batch

other_shared_work: Development tests, diagnostic scoring and later a single native allocation-benchmark child may overlap. They are not counted as screening games. No claim of exclusive whole-machine benchmarking is made.
measurement_limit: Per-bot CPU and decision/search timing are measured, but exact whole-machine CPU utilization and a complete timestamped scheduler history were not collected. Requested search effort is not actual CPU or completed work. Compare recorded visits, completed worlds, preparation and latency alongside game outcomes.
status: Live record; append later phase changes rather than rewriting prior observations.

capacity_policy_changes.previous: At most two screening batches, four games each
capacity_policy_changes.current: Global upper bound of eight long games; each manifest still allows at most four. A new four-game batch may start while old tails remain only when the sum of min(4, planned minus completed) over prior active batches is at most four. Count queued games too.
capacity_policy_changes.reason: Primary implementer approved tail overlap without changing per-manifest settings or global eight-game cap.
